question.problem: Express $\ln\left(x^2 y\right)$ as a sum of two logarithms.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the product rule for natural logarithms:

$$
\ln{a} + \ln{b} = \ln(ab)
$$

Using the product rule, the given expression can be rewritten as

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}y) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}\cdot y) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$
